images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of IntReal.IntReal-100K contains 100,000 multimodal interleaved samples with 538,452 images, curated from 7 real-world sources and organized into 4 categories. The IntReal Evaluation Suite performs coarse-to-fine diagnosis via 7 fine-grained dimensions.

Figure 2:Overview of the IntReal Evaluation Suite.We select 600 high-quality samples from IntReal-100K to construct this suite. Each sample is evaluated at two granularities: holistic evaluation generates the complete interleaved sequence at once, while fine-grained evaluation generates the next image conditioned on the preceding interleaved context to enable controllable diagnosis.

Figure 7:Case study on SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT.SFT produces more detailed text but degrades visual details (distorted brush), while RL preserves the text improvements and restores image quality.

Figure 8:Calibration case for Text Richness.A low-scoring sample fromBagel+SFT, where the response fails to provide sufficiently specific insect characteristics and offers only limited detail when distinguishing the target insect from similar species, leading to a lowText Richnessscore.
Figure 9:Calibration case for Text Logicality.A low-scoring sample fromU1-8B-MoT, where spatial and factual inconsistencies in the description lead to a lowText Logicalityscore.

Figure 10:Calibration case for Image Aesthetic.A low-scoring sample fromU1-8B-MoT-SFT, where image quality degrades over steps, with later images exhibiting excessively strong saturation and contrast and appearing less photorealistic, leading to a lowImage Aestheticscore.

Figure 11:Calibration case for Image Diversity.A low-scoring sample fromEmu3.5, where Images 1&2, 3&4, and 5&6 are excessively similar to each other, resulting in limited visual variation and a lowImage Diversityscore.

Figure 12:Calibration case for Quantity Compliance.A low-scoring sample fromBagel+SFT+RL, where the prompt requests eight images but the response generates only six, leading to a lowQuantity Compliancescore.

Figure 13:Calibration case for Context Fidelity.A low-scoring sample fromU1-8B-MoT+SFT+RL, where the generated images fail to faithfully follow the described cooking process: the bread is insufficiently toasted in the first image, while the second image omits the preparation and spreading of the caramelized onions, leading to a lowContext Fidelityscore.

Figure 14:Calibration case for Subject Consistency.A low-scoring sample fromU1-A3B-MoT, where the main subjects are not consistently preserved across images. For example, the green dinosaur differs across Images 1, 4, and 5, while the teddy bear changes color between Images 3 and 6. Since the reference sequence maintains a stable subject appearance throughout, such internal inconsistency in the generated images necessarily manifests as low similarity to the reference at the corresponding positions, leading to a low Subject Consistency score.

Figure 18:Qualitative example from the Planning category generated by Nanobanana2.The response interleaves text and images to introduce the geography, history, and landmarks of Mayfair and Marylebone.

Figure 19:Qualitative example from the Knowledge category generated by Emu3.5.The response interleaves text and images to describe the appearance, reproductive behavior, and development of the copper demoiselle damselfly.

Figure 20:Qualitative example from the Tutorial category generated by U1-8B-MoT+SFT+RL.The response interleaves text and images to explain how to roast cherry tomatoes with garlic and rosemary and serve them with bread.

Figure 21:Qualitative example from the Story category generated by Bagel+SFT+RL.The response interleaves text and images to narrate a group of dinosaurs exploring and playing together in a lush jungle.
